Antares and the Pleiades are not in the.why: People place each in its constellation, but nobody states that two unrelated objects are in different constellations. The model gets the answer by looking up Scorpius and Taurus separately and comparing them. The direct forms are absent or rare.

The brightest star in Taurus is not a re.why: Aldebaran is called a red giant or an orange giant, and Antares a red supergiant; nobody writes the negative about "the brightest star in Taurus". The model names Aldebaran and then its class. The direct form is almost absent.

The constellation whose brightest star i.why: Constellations are described by their season, and Antares by its constellation, but the description "the constellation whose brightest star is Antares" is almost never written with a season. The model resolves it to Scorpius and recalls that it belongs to the summer sky.

notes: Replaces Aldebaran/Crux: the earlier audit showed the Pioneer 10 bridges were missed by 3 of 4 models and the Chinese answer by 2, so the edit swaps two stars every model holds (Antares in Scorpius, Aldebaran in Taurus). brightest_star_in is functional and has an inverse and a subproperty: near uses the inverse, the same-constellation question uses the subproperty. The far question reaches Taurus through the Pleiades; the composed phrase is not written, so its stored claim rests on the quoted article (see the build report). The indeterminate query is a background-belief case about the eye of the Bull. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama).
